name: Legislative oversight

subjectOf.text: Error correction is weak for Member State corporate law adjudication: national legislatures are unlikely to intervene unless judicial error affects domestic interests, so managers and investors would rather face slow learning judges in their home country.
subjectOf.abstract: National legislatures could intervene and change corporate law, but unless judicial error affects domestic interests, legislatures are unlikely to do so. Managers and investors thus would probably prefer to confront slow learning judges in their home country.
subjectOf.citation: Christian Kirchner, Richard W. Painter, Wulf A. Kaal, Regulatory Competition in EU Corporate Law after Inspire Art Unbundling Delaware's Product for Euro (2004). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=617681
scope_conditions: EU level intervention being slow and therefore a weak deterrent

subjectOf.text: Automatic adjustment mechanisms trade democratic input for responsiveness: by removing policy changes from the legislative agenda they limit opportunities for public debate and scrutiny, which raises accountability and transparency concerns.
subjectOf.abstract: Another challenge is the potential reduction in legislative oversight and democratic input, as these mechanisms may limit opportunities for public debate and scrutiny of ongoing policy adjustments, raising concerns about accountability and transparency.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Future of Law - Dynamic Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4957318
scope_conditions: where adjustment is triggered automatically without legislative revisiting

description: 2 claims in the published works of Wulf A. Kaal carry the concept tag 'legislative-oversight'. Derived node: a roster, not an adjudicated definition.
